rationale:
dual_domain_bilateral_n2i-claude-agentic: train_n=200, val_n=6, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, seed=1234, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=400, outer_wall_s=3000, lr=0.005, proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=1, img_kernel=13, rationale=iter-10 CEILING-DOCUMENTATION PROBE (image-domain BF kernel SIZE / receptive field) toward the iter-20 hard stop -- NOT hr-chasing. Change EXACTLY ONE knob: img_kernel 7 -> 13 (nearly double the image-domain bilateral filter spatial support, 7x7 -> 13x13). This is a genuinely NOT-yet-tried axis: it widens the BF's effective receptive field WITHOUT adding any trainable parameters (still exactly 6: proj_n_bf=img_n_bf=1, 3 sigma each). lr reverted 0.001 -> 0.005 back to the Wagner-2022 BF CONFIG default (iter-9 confirmed lr-down is INERT on the 6-param BF: lr 5e-3->1e-3 -> 0.945747, flat hr 0; the U-Net lr-down lever does NOT transfer), so this is a clean single-knob A/B vs the iter-1 canonical config isolating the kernel-size axis. Everything else held at iter-1 canonical: warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, img_n_bf=proj_n_bf=1, all sigmas at Wagner defaults, n_iter=400, grad_clip=1.0, train_n=200, val_n=6, seed=1234 (iter-6-confirmed stable).

STATE: CONVERGED to the 6-param structural ceiling. 9 iters all flat at SSIM ~0.9457-0.9470 @1, hr 0 (PSNR ~35.6 dB, ~1 dB BELOW the LD-FBP baseline 36.56 dB): iter-1 0.946237, iter-2 (img_n_bf 1->3) 0.945237, iter-3 (img_sr 0.02->0.005) 0.946177, iter-4 (proj_sr 0.02->0.0005) 0.945745, iter-5 (warm_start OFF) 0.945955, iter-6 (seed 42->1234) 0.946157, iter-7 (pretrain_epochs 3->8) 0.946953, iter-8 (n_iter 400->800) 0.946240, iter-9 (lr 5e-3->1e-3) 0.945747. This matches the documented dd-bf-supervised structural ceiling (capped 0.9502 with the SAME 6 BF params, every scalar flat).

FAILURE MODE (structural, not a tuning miss): the 6-param bilateral cannot beat an already-clean dense-view (2304-angle) FBP -- the half-view N2I information loss (each per-scan fit only ever sees a 1152-angle subset of the scan) exceeds what 6 trainable bilateral params can denoise, so no sigma/depth/warm_start/seed/warm-start-depth/per-scan-step/lr setting clears hr=0. The remaining iters to iter-20 are CEILING DOCUMENTATION (probes that show WHY the ceiling holds), not optimization.

WHY THIS KNOB / NEW AXIS (untried): all 9 prior iters probed the OPTIMIZATION of the 6-param BF -- the sigma INITIAL VALUES (iter-2 depth, iter-3 img_sr, iter-4 proj_sr), the warm-start (presence iter-5, depth iter-7), the RNG/val-draw (iter-6), and the per-scan optimization regime (step count iter-8, lr iter-9). The BF KERNEL SIZE -- the fixed spatial support over which each trainable BF aggregates -- has stayed at the CONFIG default img_kernel=7 in ALL 9 iters. It is the one remaining untried STRUCTURAL axis that is distinct from both capacity (param count, fixed at 6) and optimization (sigma/lr/steps): it sets the BF's effective RECEPTIVE FIELD. This probe asks the sharpest possible ceiling question -- is the ~0.947 ceiling a RECEPTIVE-FIELD limit (a 7x7 window is too small to span the noise correlation length of the 2304-view FBP, escapable by a wider kernel at the same 6 params) or a true 6-PARAM-CAPACITY limit (the BF simply lacks the degrees of freedom to denoise below the FBP, independent of how far each filter reaches)? Doubling img_kernel 7->13 widens the image-domain receptive field ~2x while keeping params at exactly 6, cleanly isolating receptive field from capacity.

EXPECTATION (success condition for a ceiling-documentation probe): img_kernel 7->13 is expected to land at essentially the SAME ~0.9462 @1, hr 0. A flat result CONFIRMS the ceiling is a 6-PARAM-CAPACITY limit, NOT a receptive-field limit -- widening the BF's spatial reach does not let 6 trainable params denoise below the already-clean 2304-view FBP, bounding the ceiling along the receptive-field axis and ruling out 'kernel too small' as the cause. By construction this adds NO trainable capacity, so it cannot escape the ceiling -- it can only document its invariance to the BF receptive field. This is ceiling-documentation toward the iter-20 hard stop, not hr-chasing.

Per-image N2I (commit 1f4c3394): short amortized warm-start pre-pass (3 ep x 200 train) then per-scan Adam fit (400 steps) on each val scan's OWN half-angle measurements (GT-free), scored by evaluate_calibrated on the SAME L277 val scenes as every other Mayo method. NOT amortized train-then-forward. Wall <=15 min target: a 13x13 image BF is modestly slower per step than 7x7 but n_iter/val_n unchanged; iter-1 ran 469s at img_kernel=7/val_n=6, expect ~500-600s, within the 1h sbatch wall and the <=15 min soft target.
